heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Dominica
heroData.subtitle: Hire professionals in Dominica without a local entity
heroData.description: Comprehensive EOR services to hire compliant talent in Dominica in days, handling payroll, taxes, and benefits.
heroData.bestFor: Companies expanding to Dominica without a local entity

steps.title: Contract Issuance
steps.description: Drafting compliant employment contracts that must be provided to the employee within 14 days of the start date. Contracts must detail wages, hours, duties, and termination conditions.

steps.title: Social Security Registration
steps.description: Registering the new hire with the Dominica Social Security (DSS) within 7 days. Valid identification (passport/ID card) and proof of address are mandatory for enrollment.

steps.title: Tax Setup
steps.description: Registering the employee with the Inland Revenue Division (IRD) for Pay As You Earn (PAYE) tax withholdings based on the progressive tax rates.

steps.title: Benefits Enrollment
steps.description: Enrolling employees in statutory benefits including sick leave and maternity leave as mandated by the Labour Standards Act.

steps.title: Equipment Provision
steps.description: Arranging for the delivery and setup of necessary work equipment (laptops, monitors), subject to customs duties and clearance if imported.

rows.label: EOR Management Fee
values: Standard monthly fee per employee charged by global EOR providers.

rows.label: Employer Social Security
values: Mandatory contribution on employee earnings (includes redundancy fund portion).

rows.label: Severance Accrual
values: Recommended accrual for potential statutory severance pay (approx 1-2 weeks per year).

rows.label: Health Insurance
values: Optional private health coverage typically costs $50-$150/mo per employee.

items.title: Probationary Periods
items.text: Probation periods typically range from 1 to 3 months. Termination during this period is simpler but must still follow due process regarding notice.

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: The statutory minimum wage is EC$7.50 per hour (approx XCD 4.00), applicable to most sectors, though skilled roles command significantly higher.

items.title: Written Contracts
items.text: While oral contracts are valid, a written statement of particulars is legally required within 14 days to avoid disputes.

items.title: Work Week
items.text: Standard work week is 40 hours (8 hours/day). Overtime is paid at 1.5x regular rate, and double time on public holidays.

items.title: Valid Causes
items.text: Valid grounds include serious misconduct (theft, fraud), repeated minor misconduct (after warnings), incapacity, or redundancy.

items.title: Redundancy Process
items.text: Redundancy requires consultation. Employees with 3+ years of service are entitled to statutory redundancy pay.

items.title: Dismissal Letters
items.text: All dismissals should be confirmed in writing stating the reason, date of termination, and final payout details.

items.title: Termination Notice
items.description: Notice periods vary by tenure: 2 weeks (<1 year), 4 weeks (1-5 years), and 6 weeks (>5 years).

items.title: Severance Pay
items.description: Eligible after 3 years continuous service. Redundancy pay is generally 2 weeks/year (up to 10 years) and 3 weeks/year (10+ years), capped at 52 weeks.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.description: Employees working on public holidays are entitled to double time pay. There are typically 12 public holidays per year.

items.title: Record Retention
items.description: Employment records must be kept for at least 6 years for tax and social security audits.

items.title: Permanent Establishment
items.text: Using an EOR does not fully eliminate Permanent Establishment risks if the employee has authority to conclude contracts or is involved in revenue-generating sales activities.

items.title: IP Assignment
items.text: While EOR contracts include IP assignment clauses, specific care must be taken to ensure these hold up under Dominica's intellectual property laws for foreign entities.

items.title: Shadow Payroll
items.text: It is critical to ensure that any stock options or global benefits provided directly by the parent company are reported for local tax withholding.

faqs.question: Is independent contractor engagement risky?
faqs.answer: Yes, misclassification risk exists. If a contractor acts like an employee (fixed hours, supervision), they may be deemed an employee by labor tribunals.

faqs.question: Can I hire foreigners via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the EOR must sponsor a work permit, which is granted only if no local talent is available.

faqs.question: What is the currency for payroll?
faqs.answer: Payroll is typically processed in Eastern Caribbean Dollars (XCD), though contracts can be denominated in USD.

steps.title: Data Aggregation
steps.description: Collecting time sheets, overtime hours, and any bonus approvals by the 20th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculating PAYE tax, Social Security deductions (capped at ceiling), and net pay.

steps.title: Tax Filing
steps.description: Submitting PAYE returns to the Inland Revenue Division and Social Security contributions to DSS by the end of the month.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Transferring net salaries to employee bank accounts via local banking networks.

steps.title: Payslip Delivery
steps.description: Distributing electronic or physical payslips to employees as required by law.

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 12 weeks of leave. Employers must pay 50% of wages for 4 weeks. DSS pays a maternity benefit (60%) for up to 3 months if eligible.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.text: Up to 6 weeks per year with medical certificate. Employer pays the difference between DSS sickness benefit and full salary.

items.title: Vacation Leave
items.text: 2 weeks per year (years 1-5), increasing to 3 weeks (year 5+). Accrued leave must be paid out on termination.

items.title: Filing Deadlines
items.text: PAYE and Social Security payments are strictly due by the 14th of the following month. Late fees include 10% penalty plus interest.

items.title: Tax Free Allowance
items.text: The first EC$30,000 of annual income is tax-free for residents (approx EC$2,500/month).

items.title: Bonus Treatment
items.text: Bonuses are fully taxable and subject to Social Security deductions unless the yearly ceiling is reached.

items.title: 13th Month Pay
items.text: Not legally mandatory, but customary in some industries as a Christmas bonus.

items.title: Record Keeping
items.description: Payroll records must be maintained for 7 years.

items.title: E-Filing
items.description: The IRD portal allows for electronic submission of monthly remittance forms.

items.title: Benefits in Kind
items.description: Housing and vehicle allowances are taxable benefits and must be included in gross income.

faqs.question: What is the employer's total social security cost?
faqs.answer: The employer contributes 7.75% of the employee's insurable earnings, up to the ceiling of $7,000 XCD/month.

faqs.question: Are benefits in kind taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, non-cash benefits like housing or vehicle allowances are generally taxable.

faqs.question: How do I pay the authorities?
faqs.answer: Payments can be made online via the IRD portal or at physical tax offices.

items.title: Tax Free Threshold
items.text: Ensure the first 30,000 XCD is excluded from tax calculations.

items.title: Ceilings
items.text: Social security deductions are capped at insurable earnings of $7,000 XCD per month.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Calculations should be done in XCD. Fixed peg is 2.70 XCD = 1 USD.

items.title: Redundancy
items.text: The 7.75% employer contribution includes the redundancy fund portion.

steps.title: Gross Pay
steps.description: Determine the gross monthly salary including any taxable allowances.

steps.title: Social Security
steps.description: Deduct employee contribution (6.75%) from gross pay (capped at $7,000 XCD).

steps.title: Tax (PAYE)
steps.description: Calculate income tax on the taxable income (Gross - Social Security - Personal Allowance).

steps.title: Net Pay
steps.description: Subtract all deductions from gross pay to arrive at the net amount payable.

faqs.question: Is the tax allowance monthly?
faqs.answer: It is an annual allowance (30,000), usually pro-rated monthly (2,500) for PAYE.

faqs.question: Are foreign earnings taxed?
faqs.answer: For residents, yes. Double taxation relief may apply if a treaty exists.

faqs.question: Does this include health insurance?
faqs.answer: No, specific private health insurance is effectively a separate benefit.

steps.description: Drafting Articles of Incorporation and By-laws, and obtaining notarized IDs for directors.

steps.title: Fee Payment

items.title: Tax Holidays
items.text: Under the Fiscal Incentives Act, approved enterprises (e.g., manufacturing, tourism) can receive tax holidays of up to 15 years.

items.title: Duty Waivers
items.text: Exemptions on import duties for plant, machinery, and raw materials for qualifying projects.

items.title: Hotels Aid Act
items.text: Specific incentives for hotel construction and expansion, including 10-20 year tax holidays.

items.title: Timeframe
items.text: Standard incubation takes 1-2 weeks. IBCs can often be formed faster (24-48 hours).

items.title: Bank Accounts
items.text: Opening a corporate bank account can take significantly longer (4-8 weeks) due to strict KYC/AML checks.

items.title: Registered Office
items.text: A physical local address is required for the registered office; a P.O. Box alone is insufficient.

items.title: Directors
items.text: Minimum of one director is required. Corporate directors are permitted for IBCs.

items.title: Investment Options
items.text: Two main routes exist: A non-refundable contribution to the Economic Diversification Fund (min $200,000 USD) or an investment in government-approved real estate (min $200,000 USD).

items.title: Real Estate Holding
items.text: Approved real estate must be held for a minimum of 3 years. If the property is sold to another CBI applicant, the holding period increases to 5 years.

items.title: Due Diligence Fees
items.text: Strict diligence checks apply. Fees are approximately $7,500 for the main applicant and $4,000 for dependents over 16.

items.title: Key Benefits
items.text: Citizenship grants visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to over 140 countries, including the Schengen Area, and requires no minimum physical residency.

faqs.question: Do I need to be in Dominica to incorporate?
faqs.answer: No, the process can be handled remotely through a registered agent.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital?
faqs.answer: For private companies, there is no strict minimum, but IBCs typically start with nominal capital (e.g., $100 USD).

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100% of the shares?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is permitted.

items.title: Relationships First
items.text: Building personal rapport is often a prerequisite to business. Initial meetings often involve small talk about family, sports (cricket), or local events.

items.title: Formal Greetings
items.text: Address counterparts by their title and surname (e.g., Mr. Charles) unless invited to use first names. A firm handshake is the standard greeting.

items.title: Dress Code
items.text: Business attire is conservative despite the tropical climate. Lightweight suits for men and professional dresses or suits for women are expected.

items.title: Time Management
items.text: While foreign visitors are expected to be punctual, be prepared for a more relaxed approach to time ('island time') from local counterparts.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must demonstrate that no suitable local candidate was found (Labour Market Test).

faqs.question: Are background checks legal?

faqs.question: What is the standard vacation time?
faqs.answer: 2 weeks for less than 5 years of service, 3 weeks for 5+ years.

items.title: Economic Substance

items.title: Late Penalties

items.title: Best Practice

items.title: Consumer Rights

faqs.question: What is the FIU?
faqs.answer: The Financial Intelligence Unit is the national agency responsible for receiving and analyzing financial information related to crime.

faqs.question: Are directors liable?
faqs.answer: Yes, directors can be held personally liable for the company's failure to comply with certain statutory obligations.

faqs.question: How often must we update KYC?

items.title: Registration Threshold
items.text: Registration is mandatory for businesses with turnover > EC$250,000 (EC$62,500 for tourism providers).

items.title: Zero-Rated Items
items.text: Basic food (rice, milk, flour), fuel, and exports are zero-rated (0% VAT).

items.title: Exempt Supplies
items.text: Residential rent, financial services, and education services are exempt from VAT.

items.title: Exempt Supplies
items.text: Certain services are exempt from VAT, including residential rent, financial services, medical services, and educational services. Input tax cannot be recovered.

items.title: Zero-Rated Goods
items.text: Zero-rated items (0% VAT) include basic food staples (rice, flour, milk, sugar), fuel, agricultural inputs, and exported goods.

items.title: Tourism Incentives
items.text: A reduced VAT rate of 10% applies specifically to hotel accommodation and diving services to support the tourism sector.

items.title: Filing Deadline
items.text: Corporate returns are due by March 31st (or 3 months after fiscal year end).

items.title: Quarterly Installments
items.text: Tax is payable in quarterly installments based on the previous year's liability.

items.title: Tax Holidays
items.text: Fiscal incentives are available for approved tourism and manufacturing projects (up to 20 years for some).

items.title: Worldwide Income
items.text: Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents only on Dominica-sourced income.

items.title: Capital Allowances
items.text: Depreciation is a deductible expense. Accelerated depreciation may be granted for qualifying capital investments.

items.title: No Capital Gains Tax
items.text: There is no general capital gains tax in Dominica, making asset appreciation tax-efficient.

items.title: Loss Carry Forward
items.text: Net losses can generally be carried forward to offset future profits, subject to specific rules.

faqs.answer: Generally, there is no capital gains tax in Dominica, except in specific land transfer contexts.

faqs.question: Can I offset losses?

faqs.question: What about double taxation?
faqs.answer: Dominica has double taxation treaties with CARICOM members and some other nations.
